evidence.quote: | NetEndOfMonth days -> DateOnly(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month, DateTime.DaysInMonth(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month)).AddDays days

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new due-date rule is in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The terms-parsing and validation rule (1 to 365 days, EOM suffix) is in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2). The Tier 3 and Tier 4 code is untouched, and the Tier 2 storage codec only maps the new case to JSON and back.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no clock, randomness, I/O or console use. The due date is computed purely from the issue date, and `DateTime.DaysInMonth` is a pure calendar function. The storage change only encodes and decodes the new case as a value.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The "Net N EOM" wording is written as a literal in two places, `Documents.termsText` and `Invoicing.termsWords`. The two copies agree. The 365-day limit is also checked in two separate branches of the parser, with the same value. The due-date rule, the JSON kind and the refusal message each have a single definition.

evidence.quote: | true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule and the ordinal wording are in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The parsing and the 1 to 28 range check are in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2). Tier 3 and Tier 4 only call these and decide nothing. The storage codec only carries the value.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effects. `ordinal` and the due-date calculation are pure, and the parsing is pure code in the engine. The storage change only encodes and decodes the new case as a value.

evidence.quote: | DayOfNextMonth day -> $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"
| Some(DayOfNextMonth day) -> $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: `ordinal` has one definition, in Invoicing, and both call sites use it. The "Due the Nth of next month" template is still written twice, once in `termsText` and once in `termsWords`, and the copies agree. The "Net N EOM" literal is also still duplicated from change set 1. The refusal message is a single local binding that was updated in place, and the 1 to 28 range is defined once, in the parser.
